accelerator:fermilab-booster.summary_technical: 474 m circumference rapid-cycling synchrotron running at 15 Hz, accelerating protons from 400 MeV to 8 GeV kinetic energy (8.89 GeV/c) for the BNB and for injection into the Recycler and Main Injector.

accelerator:fermilab-linac.summary_technical: 201.25 MHz normal-conducting H- linac delivering 400 MeV to the Booster; to be replaced by the 800 MeV PIP-II superconducting linac.

notes: Design energy 150 GeV per the NuMI beam paper; 120 GeV is the neutrino-production operating point.
accelerator:fermilab-main-injector.summary_technical: 3.3 km circumference proton synchrotron, design energy 150 GeV, operated at 120 GeV for neutrino production; slip-stacked Booster batches are loaded via the Recycler. Source of the NuMI beam and of the future LBNF beam.

accelerator:fermilab-pip-ii.summary_technical: 800 MeV CW-capable superconducting RF H- linac replacing the 400 MeV normal-conducting linac, injecting into the Booster and enabling 1.2 MW of 60-120 GeV protons on the LBNF target.

accelerator:fermilab-recycler.summary_technical: 8 GeV permanent-magnet storage ring in the Main Injector tunnel (3.3 km). Built for Tevatron Run II antiproton storage, now used for Booster-batch stacking and slip stacking ahead of Main Injector acceleration.

accelerator:fermilab-tevatron.summary_technical: Superconducting proton-antiproton collider, 980 GeV per beam (1.96 TeV centre of mass in Run II, 2002-2011); collider operation from December 1985 to the September 2011 shutdown. Host of CDF and DZero.

result:belle-b-to-tau-nu-evidence-2006.why_it_matters: A tree-level, helicity-suppressed decay sensitive to charged-Higgs exchange; the first direct measurement of f_B|V_ub|.

claim.quote: Observation of Large CP Violation in the Neutral B Meson System

notes: Companion measurement to BaBar's contemporaneous result; that is not recorded here.
result:belle-cp-violation-observation-20.summary_technical: Time-dependent measurement of CP asymmetry in B⁰ → (cc̅)K⁰ and related modes at the Υ(4S), giving sin 2φ₁ = 0.99 ± 0.14(stat) ± 0.06(syst) and excluding the CP-conserving hypothesis.
result:belle-cp-violation-observation-20.why_it_matters: Established CP violation in the B system and validated the Kobayashi-Maskawa mechanism as the dominant source of CP violation in quark flavour transitions.

claim.quote: Evidence for $D^0 - \bar{D}^0$ Mixing

result:belle-d0-mixing-evidence-2007.summary_technical: Measurement of y_CP = (1.31 ± 0.32(stat) ± 0.25(syst))% from lifetime differences between CP-eigenstate and flavour-eigenstate D⁰ decays in 540 fb⁻¹, 3.2σ from zero, with no evidence for CP violation.
result:belle-d0-mixing-evidence-2007.why_it_matters: Completed the picture of neutral-meson mixing: mixing is now established in the K, B, B_s and D systems, and charm mixing is a sensitive probe of new physics in the up-quark sector.

claim.quote: we determine the branching fraction of the decay $B^{+}\rightarrow K^{+}\nu\bar{\nu}$ to be $[2.3 \pm 0.5(\mathrm{stat})^{+0.5}_{-0.4}(\mathrm{syst})]\times 10^{-5}$, providing the first evidence for this decay at $3.5$ standard deviations.

notes: The collaboration's own word is 'evidence'; the paper is not described as an observation.
result:belle-ii-b-to-k-nunu-evidence-202.summary_technical: Inclusive-tag and hadronic-tag searches in 362 fb⁻¹ at the Υ(4S) combine to B(B⁺ → K⁺ νν̅) = [2.3 ± 0.5(stat) ⁺⁰·⁵₋₀.₄(syst)] × 10⁻⁵, the first evidence for the decay at 3.5σ and 2.7σ above the Standard Model expectation.
result:belle-ii-b-to-k-nunu-evidence-202.why_it_matters: A flavour-changing neutral current with a clean theoretical prediction; the mild excess over the Standard Model has become one of the most watched flavour anomalies.

claim.quote: we measure the $τ$ mass to be $1777.09 ± 0.08 ± 0.11 \,\mathrm{MeV\!/c^2}$, where the first uncertainty is statistical and the second systematic. This result is the most precise to date.

notes: Journal publication was not confirmed on a source fetched in this session.
result:belle-ii-tau-mass-measurement-202.summary_technical: Pseudomass-endpoint measurement in τ⁻ → π⁻π⁺π⁻ ν_τ using ~175 million e⁺e⁻ → τ⁺τ⁻ events in 190 fb⁻¹ at √s = 10.579 GeV, giving m_τ = 1777.09 ± 0.08(stat) ± 0.11(syst) MeV/c².
result:belle-ii-tau-mass-measurement-202.why_it_matters: The tau mass enters tests of lepton universality and of the Standard Model's lepton sector; this measurement was the most precise at the time of publication.

claim.quote: We report the observation of a narrow charmonium-like state produced in the exclusive decay process B+ -> K+ pi+pi- J/psi.

result:belle-x3872-observation-2003.summary_technical: Observation of a narrow state decaying to π⁺π⁻ J/ψ in B⁺ → K⁺ π⁺π⁻ J/ψ, mass 3872.0 ± 0.6(stat) ± 0.5(syst) MeV, very close to the D⁰D̅*⁰ threshold, with a statistical significance in excess of 10σ in 152M BB̅ events.
result:belle-x3872-observation-2003.why_it_matters: First of the 'XYZ' exotic hadrons; its proximity to the D⁰D̅*⁰ threshold drove a generation of work on molecular and tetraquark interpretations.

claim.quote: An excess of events is observed above the expected background, with a local significance of 5.0 standard deviations, at a mass near 125 GeV, signalling the production of a new particle.

notes: The collaboration wording is "observation of a new boson", not "discovery of the Higgs boson"; the identification with the standard model Higgs boson came later.
result:cms-higgs-boson-observation-2012.summary_technical: Combined search in the gamma gamma, ZZ, WW, tau tau and bb channels using up to 5.1 fb^-1 at 7 TeV and 5.3 fb^-1 at 8 TeV; local significance 5.0 sigma at m = 125.3 +/- 0.4 (stat.) +/- 0.5 (syst.) GeV.
result:cms-higgs-boson-observation-2012.why_it_matters: The Higgs boson is the particle associated with the field that gives elementary particles their masses; its observation completed the standard model and opened a new field of precision Higgs measurements.

claim.quote: Here the CMS Collaboration reports the most up-to-date combination of results on the properties of the Higgs boson, including the most stringent limit on the cross section for the production of a pair of Higgs bosons, on the basis of data from proton-proton collisions at a centre-of-mass energy of 13 TeV.

result:cms-higgs-boson-portrait-2022.summary_technical: Combination of CMS 13 TeV Higgs measurements: production cross sections in all main modes, fermionic and bosonic decay channels, spin-parity, mass, and the most stringent limit at the time on Higgs boson pair production.
result:cms-higgs-boson-portrait-2022.why_it_matters: It is the most complete single-experiment statement of what the Higgs boson is, and the baseline that HL-LHC measurements will be compared against.

claim.quote: The combination of this result with searches by the CMS experiment for H $\to\mathrm{b\overline{b}}$ in other production processes yields an observed (expected) significance of 5.6 (5.5) standard deviations and a signal strength of 1.04 $\pm$ 0.20.

result:cms-higgs-to-bb-observation-2018.summary_technical: VH production with 41.3 fb^-1 of 2017 data gives 4.8 sigma at m_H = 125.09 GeV; combined with 7, 8 and 13 TeV VH data and with other production modes the observed (expected) significance is 5.6 (5.5) sigma, signal strength 1.04 +/- 0.20.
result:cms-higgs-to-bb-observation-2018.why_it_matters: H -> bb is the dominant Higgs decay; observing it at the predicted rate confirmed the standard model picture of how the Higgs boson decays.

claim.quote: The combination with the corresponding measurement performed with data collected by the CMS experiment at center-of-mass energies of 7 and 8 TeV leads to an observed significance of 5.9 standard deviations, equal to the expected significance.

result:cms-higgs-to-tau-tau-observation-.summary_technical: 35.9 fb^-1 at 13 TeV gives 4.9 sigma for H -> tau tau; combining with 7 and 8 TeV data gives 5.9 sigma and a signal strength of 1.09 +0.27 -0.26 times the standard model expectation.
result:cms-higgs-to-tau-tau-observation-.why_it_matters: It was the first direct observation of the Higgs boson coupling to fermions by a single experiment, testing whether the Higgs gives mass to matter particles as predicted.

claim.quote: These provide the most stringent lower limits to date on the masses for various spin-1 particles, spin-2 gravitons in the Randall--Sundrum model, as well as spin-1 mediators between the SM and dark matter particles.

notes: Numerical mass limits are quoted in the body of the paper, not in the abstract that was fetched, so no key_value is recorded.
result:cms-high-mass-dilepton-search-202.summary_technical: Dielectron and dimuon mass spectra from up to 140 fb^-1 of 13 TeV data: no significant deviation from the standard model; limits on narrow spin-1 and spin-2 resonances, dark matter mediators, contact interactions and ADD large extra dimensions, plus a TeV-scale test of lepton flavour universality.
result:cms-high-mass-dilepton-search-202.why_it_matters: High-mass dilepton searches are the cleanest and most far-reaching direct probe of new heavy particles at the LHC; the null result constrains many extensions of the standard model at once.

claim.quote: The combined analysis produces the first observation of the $B^0_s\to\mu^+\mu^-$ decay, with a statistical significance exceeding six standard deviations, and the best measurement of its branching fraction so far.

notes: A joint CMS + LHCb result. collaboration:lhcb is outside this workstream and is not referenced as an id.
result:cms-lhcb-bs-to-mumu-observation-2.summary_technical: Joint CMS+LHCb analysis of 7 and 8 TeV data: first observation of B0s -> mu+mu- at >6 sigma, plus 3 sigma evidence for B0 -> mu+mu-; branching fractions compatible with the standard model.
result:cms-lhcb-bs-to-mumu-observation-2.why_it_matters: The decay is strongly suppressed in the standard model, so its rate is one of the sharpest constraints on new heavy particles in flavour physics.

claim.quote: This is the first observation of such a long-range, near-side feature in two-particle correlation functions in pp or p p-bar collisions.

result:cms-long-range-near-side-correlat.summary_technical: Two-particle Delta(eta)-Delta(phi) correlations in 7 TeV pp collisions show a pronounced near-side ridge at 2.0 < |Delta(eta)| < 4.8 for 1-3 GeV/c tracks in high-multiplicity events (980 nb^-1).
result:cms-long-range-near-side-correlat.why_it_matters: The ridge is a signature previously associated with the quark-gluon plasma; seeing it in proton-proton collisions raised the question of whether collective behaviour also arises in the smallest collision systems.

claim.quote: The top quark mass is measured to be 171.77 $\pm$ 0.37 GeV.

result:cms-top-quark-mass-measurement-20.summary_technical: 36.3 fb^-1 at 13 TeV, lepton+jets ttbar candidates, kinematic fit plus a profile likelihood over up to four observables: m_t = 171.77 +/- 0.37 GeV.
result:cms-top-quark-mass-measurement-20.why_it_matters: The top quark mass enters the electroweak fit and the stability of the Higgs potential, so every improvement in its precision sharpens tests of the standard model.

claim.quote: An excess of events is observed, with a significance of 5.2 standard deviations, over the expectation from the background-only hypothesis.

result:cms-tth-observation-2018.summary_technical: Combination of ttH searches in WW, ZZ, gamma gamma, tau tau and bb final states at 7, 8 and 13 TeV (up to 5.1, 19.7 and 35.9 fb^-1): 5.2 sigma observed, 4.2 sigma expected, signal strength 1.26 +0.31 -0.26.
result:cms-tth-observation-2018.why_it_matters: The top quark Yukawa coupling is the largest in the standard model and is sensitive to new physics; measuring it directly tests the Higgs mechanism where it matters most.

claim.quote: we reach a precise measurement of the W mass, of 80 360.2 ± 9.9 MeV, in agreement with the standard model prediction.

result:cms-w-boson-mass-measurement-2024.summary_technical: W -> mu nu events from 2016 13 TeV data, high-granularity maximum likelihood fit to muon kinematics with in situ constraints on theory inputs: m_W = 80 360.2 +/- 9.9 MeV.
result:cms-w-boson-mass-measurement-2024.why_it_matters: The W and Z masses are related in the standard model, so a precise W mass is a sensitive probe of undiscovered heavy particles entering through quantum loops.

claim.quote: The excavation of the caverns that will house the gigantic particle detectors of the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment in Lead, South Dakota is complete.

notes: Two related Fermilab announcements are cited: the 1 February 2024 completion-of-excavation press release (used for the result date) and the 15 August 2024 underground ribbon-cutting event marking the same milestone publicly; both describe the same excavation completion, not two separate results.
DUNE has published no oscillation-physics result to date, so this milestone and the ProtoDUNE-SP performance paper are the only DUNE entries in results/ (task scope note).
result:dune-far-site-excavation-2024.summary_technical: Excavation of the three DUNE far-detector caverns at the 4850-foot level of SURF, announced complete by Fermilab on 1 February 2024, four years after tunnelling work began; a formal ribbon-cutting event followed on 15 August 2024.
result:dune-far-site-excavation-2024.why_it_matters: Completing the excavation cleared the way for detector installation to begin, the last major civil-construction milestone before DUNE's far detector modules could be assembled underground.

claim.quote: First results on ProtoDUNE-SP liquid argon time projection chamber performance from a beam test at the CERN Neutrino Platform

notes: date_kind is publication: JINST 15 (2020) P12004; the arXiv preprint (2007.06722) was posted in July 2020.
This is a construction/technology milestone, not a physics discovery, evidence claim or measurement; DUNE has not yet published an oscillation-physics result (task scope note).
result:dune-protodune-sp-performance-202.summary_technical: ProtoDUNE-SP (NP04), a 770 t single-phase LArTPC built at the CERN Neutrino Platform, was exposed to a charged-particle beam of 0.3-7 GeV/c; the paper reports the detector's first operational performance (drift, purity, calorimetric response) validating the technology for the DUNE far-detector modules.
result:dune-protodune-sp-performance-202.why_it_matters: ProtoDUNE-SP proved that DUNE's single-phase liquid-argon TPC technology works at close to full detector-module scale before the collaboration committed to building the far-detector modules underground at SURF.

claim.quote: No new physics signal is observed, and we set world-leading limits on heavy QCD axions, as well as for the Higgs portal scalar among dedicated searches.

notes: This is ICARUS's first published physics result from its Fermilab SBN run (data taking began 5 November 2021); it uses the off-axis NuMI beam rather than the on-axis BNB beam used for the sterile-neutrino search.
result:icarus-hidden-sector-scalar-limit.summary_technical: Search for long-lived hidden-sector particles (heavy QCD axions, Higgs-portal scalars) produced in K -> pi + LLP decays and decaying to mu+mu- inside ICARUS-T600, using 2.41x10^20 POT from the off-axis NuMI beam at Fermilab. No signal observed; sets world-leading limits among dedicated searches for these two models.
result:icarus-hidden-sector-scalar-limit.why_it_matters: This is ICARUS's first published physics result since its move to Fermilab, demonstrating the refurbished T600's ability to search for physics beyond sterile neutrinos (hidden-sector long-lived particles) using the NuMI beam in addition to its primary BNB-based sterile-neutrino programme.

claim.quote: we constrain the atmospheric neutrino mixing parameters to be $\sin^2\theta_{23} = 0.51\pm 0.05$ and $\Delta m^2_{32} = 2.41\pm0.07\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{eV}^2$, assuming a normal mass ordering.

result:icecube-deepcore-atmospheric-osci.summary_technical: Three-flavour atmospheric oscillation fit to 2011–2019 DeepCore data with improved calibration and processing: sin²θ₂₃ = 0.51 ± 0.05 and Δm²₃₂ = (2.41 ± 0.07) × 10⁻³ eV² for normal ordering, a 40% error reduction over the previous IceCube result.
result:icecube-deepcore-atmospheric-osci.why_it_matters: Shows that a cubic-kilometre astrophysical neutrino telescope can compete with dedicated accelerator oscillation experiments, with different systematics.

claim.quote: Evidence for High-Energy Extraterrestrial Neutrinos at the IceCube Detector

result:icecube-evidence-extraterrestrial.summary_technical: All-sky search for high-energy neutrino interactions starting inside the detector, May 2010 – May 2012. Twenty-eight events between ~30 TeV and 1.2 PeV reject a purely atmospheric origin at 4σ, with flavours, directions and energies consistent with an extraterrestrial component.
result:icecube-evidence-extraterrestrial.why_it_matters: Opened high-energy neutrino astronomy: the first evidence for a diffuse flux of neutrinos of astrophysical origin.

claim.quote: We identify neutrino emission from the Galactic plane at the 4.5$\sigma$ level of significance, by comparing diffuse emission models to a background-only hypothesis.

result:icecube-galactic-plane-neutrinos-.summary_technical: Machine-learning cascade selection applied to ten years of IceCube data identifies diffuse Galactic-plane neutrino emission at 4.5σ against a background-only hypothesis; consistent with modelled diffuse emission but also compatible with unresolved point sources.
result:icecube-galactic-plane-neutrinos-.why_it_matters: First observation of neutrinos from the Milky Way, connecting Galactic cosmic rays to their interactions with interstellar matter.

claim.quote: Here we report the detection by the IceCube neutrino observatory of a cascade of high-energy particles (a particle shower) consistent with being created at the Glashow resonance.

result:icecube-glashow-resonance-candida.summary_technical: A cascade of 6.05 ± 0.72 PeV reconstructed energy, with secondary-muon features indicating hadronic decay of a resonant W⁻ boson, consistent with the Glashow resonance at 6.3 PeV antineutrino energy. Implies electron antineutrinos in the astrophysical flux.
result:icecube-glashow-resonance-candida.why_it_matters: First candidate observation of the Glashow resonance, a 60-year-old Standard Model prediction, and a way to distinguish neutrinos from antineutrinos in astrophysical fluxes.

claim.quote: We found an excess of $79_{-20}^{+22}$ neutrinos associated with the nearby active galaxy NGC 1068 at a significance of 4.2$\,\sigma$.

result:icecube-ngc-1068-evidence-2022.summary_technical: Point-source search over 2011–2020 data with improved reconstruction and calibration; 110 a priori gamma-ray sources analysed. An excess of 79(+22/-20) neutrinos at NGC 1068 with 4.2σ significance; the inferred TeV neutrino flux exceeds the TeV gamma-ray flux by at least an order of magnitude.
result:icecube-ngc-1068-evidence-2022.why_it_matters: First steady neutrino source candidate and evidence that neutrinos escape from environments opaque to gamma rays, probing the obscured core of an active galaxy.

claim.quote: The best-fit point is found to be at $\sin^2(2\theta_{24})=0.10$ and $\Delta m_{41}^2 = 4.5{\rm eV}^2$, which is consistent with the no sterile neutrino hypothesis with a p-value of 8.0\%.

result:icecube-sterile-neutrino-search-2.summary_technical: 3+1 sterile-neutrino search using 305,735 atmospheric muon neutrino events over eight years, testing matter-enhanced oscillations for Δm²₄₁ between 0.01 and 100 eV². Best fit sin²(2θ₂₄) = 0.10, Δm²₄₁ = 4.5 eV², consistent with no sterile neutrino at a p-value of 8.0%.
result:icecube-sterile-neutrino-search-2.why_it_matters: The strongest test of eV-scale sterile neutrinos through matter-enhanced oscillations in the Earth, constraining the interpretation of short-baseline anomalies.

claim.quote: This observation of a neutrino in spatial coincidence with a gamma-ray emitting blazar during an active phase suggests that blazars may be a source of high-energy neutrinos.

notes: The paper is authored jointly by IceCube and the Fermi-LAT, MAGIC, AGILE, ASAS-SN, HAWC, H.E.S.S., INTEGRAL, Kanata, Kiso, Kapteyn, Liverpool, Subaru, Swift/NuSTAR, VERITAS and VLA teams; only collaboration:icecube exists in the atlas so far.
result:icecube-txs-0506-056-multimesseng.summary_technical: The 290 TeV track alert IceCube-170922A was spatially coincident with the flaring gamma-ray blazar TXS 0506+056. A multiwavelength campaign across radio to VHE gamma rays characterised the flare, including the first VHE gamma-ray detection of the source.
result:icecube-txs-0506-056-multimesseng.why_it_matters: First identification of a candidate astrophysical source of high-energy neutrinos and a founding result of multimessenger astronomy with neutrinos.

claim.quote: Allowing for time-variable flux, this constitutes 3.5{\sigma} evidence for neutrino emission from the direction of TXS 0506+056, independent of and prior to the 2017 flaring episode.

result:icecube-txs-0506-056-prior-neutri.summary_technical: Archival time-dependent point-source search of 9.5 years of IceCube data at the position of TXS 0506+056 finds an excess between September 2014 and March 2015 at 3.5σ for a time-variable flux hypothesis.
result:icecube-txs-0506-056-prior-neutri.why_it_matters: Independent, archival evidence that blazars are sources of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos.

claim.quote: We present measurements of nu_mu disappearance in K2K, the KEK to Kamioka long-baseline neutrino oscillation experiment. ... The probability that the observations are explained by the expectation for no neutrino oscillation is 0.0015% (4.3sigma).

result:k2k-oscillation-measurement-2006.summary_technical: 112 observed vs. 158.1(+9.2/-8.6) expected beam-originated events in the SK fiducial volume, plus a distorted energy spectrum in 58 single-ring muon-like events; no-oscillation hypothesis excluded at 4.3 sigma; two-flavour fit gives Delta m^2 in [1.9,3.5]e-3 eV^2 (90% CL), best fit 2.8e-3 eV^2.
result:k2k-oscillation-measurement-2006.why_it_matters: First confirmation of neutrino oscillation using an artificial, well-characterised accelerator beam rather than natural atmospheric or solar neutrinos, validating the interpretation of the atmospheric-neutrino anomaly and establishing the long-baseline accelerator method used ever since (K2K, MINOS, T2K, NOvA, DUNE).

claim.quote: Observation of a neutrino burst from the supernova SN1987A

result:kamiokande-sn1987a-1987.summary_technical: Kamiokande-II recorded a 13-second burst of neutrino events on 23 February 1987, 7:35:35 UT, coincident with the optical detection of supernova SN 1987A in the Large Magellanic Cloud, confirming core-collapse supernova neutrino emission and opening neutrino astronomy of transient sources.
result:kamiokande-sn1987a-1987.why_it_matters: The first (and to date only) detection of neutrinos from a supernova outside the Solar System, confirming core-collapse theory and founding supernova/multimessenger neutrino astronomy; part of the work recognised by the 2002 Nobel Prize in Physics to Masatoshi Koshiba.

claim.quote: We report on the final electroweak measurements performed with data taken at the Z resonance by the experiments operating at the electron-positron colliders SLC and LEP.

notes: SLD (SLC Large Detector) is one of the five contributing experiments/collaborations in this combination but is outside the scope of this workstream (not a CERN experiment) and is not listed in experiment_ids/collaboration_ids; only the four LEP experiments are recorded here.
result:lep-electroweak-precision-2006.summary_technical: ALEPH, DELPHI, L3, OPAL and SLD combination, Phys. Rept. 427 (2006) 257-454 (arXiv:hep-ex/0509008); the final electroweak measurements at the Z resonance from LEP and SLC, including the Z mass and width, asymmetries and the number of light neutrino species (2.9840+/-0.0082).
result:lep-electroweak-precision-2006.why_it_matters: Turned a decade of LEP and SLC running into the definitive precision test of the electroweak Standard Model, constraining the top-quark and Higgs-boson masses before either was directly measured/discovered and setting the benchmark every later collider measurement is checked against.

claim.quote: A lower bound of 114.4 GeV/c2 is established, at the 95% confidence level, on the mass of the Standard Model Higgs boson.

result:lep-higgs-exclusion-2003.summary_technical: ALEPH, DELPHI, L3, OPAL and LEP Higgs Working Group combination, Phys. Lett. B 565 (2003) 61-75 (arXiv:hep-ex/0306033); a lower bound of 114.4 GeV/c^2 at 95% confidence level on the Standard Model Higgs boson mass, from the combined LEP2 direct-search data.
result:lep-higgs-exclusion-2003.why_it_matters: Set the strongest lower bound on the Higgs boson mass before the LHC era, ruling out a large swath of parameter space and shaping the design and early-run strategy of the LHC's own Higgs search.

claim.locator: ALEPH paper title, Phys.Lett.B 231 (1989) 519, INSPIRE recid 282904
claim.quote: Determination of the Number of Light Neutrino Species

notes: This entity records the historic 1989 determination that Nu=3; the final precision value (2.9840+/-0.0082) is reused here from the 2006 combination paper (also recorded separately as result:lep-electroweak-precision-2006) because no more precise 1989-dated combined figure was found in this session's sources. date/date_kind reflect the 1989 papers; key_value reflects the best available number.

ALEPH's own paper title is used as claim.quote because it states the result plainly ('Determination of the Number of Light Neutrino Species'); L3, DELPHI and OPAL used different titles for the same Z-lineshape analysis (see key_value_text).
result:lep-three-neutrino-species-1989.summary_technical: In October 1989 ALEPH, DELPHI, L3 and OPAL each independently measured the invisible partial width of the Z resonance and reported a number of light neutrino species (Nu) consistent with 3: ALEPH Nu=3.27+/-0.30, L3 Nu=3.42+/-0.48, DELPHI Nu=2.4+/-0.4(stat)+/-0.5(syst), OPAL Nu=3.1+/-0.4, each in Phys. Lett. B231 (1989) 509-547. The combined final LEP+SLD precision value, Nu=2.9840+/-0.0082, was published later in Phys. Rept. 427 (2006) 257.
result:lep-three-neutrino-species-1989.why_it_matters: Ruled out a fourth generation of ordinary matter with a light neutrino, fixing the number of families of fundamental fermions at three and shaping every particle-physics model since.

claim.quote: At a WIMP mass of 50 GeV/c^2, WIMP-nucleon spin-independent cross sections above 2.2e-46 cm^2 are excluded at the 90% confidence level. When combined with the previously reported LUX exposure, this exclusion strengthens to 1.1e-46 cm^2 at 50 GeV/c^2.

notes: significance is null: this is an exclusion limit.
result:lux-complete-exposure-2016.summary_technical: Complete LUX exposure: 3.35e4 kg day (WS2013 85.3 live days plus WS2014-16 332.0 live days, 11 Sep 2014 - 2 May 2016) with 250 kg active mass. No WIMP nuclear recoils; 90% CL spin-independent limit 2.2e-46 cm2 at 50 GeV/c2, strengthening to 1.1e-46 cm2 when combined with WS2013.
result:lux-complete-exposure-2016.why_it_matters: The final LUX exposure was the strongest direct-detection limit before the multi-tonne generation, and set the bar that LZ was built to beat.

claim.quote: allowing 90% confidence limits to be set on spin-independent WIMP-nucleon elastic scattering with a minimum upper limit on the cross section of 7.6 × 10⁻⁴⁶ cm² at a WIMP mass of 33 GeV/c²

notes: significance is null: this is an exclusion limit.
result:lux-first-wimp-search-2013.summary_technical: WS2013: 85.3 live days, 118 kg fiducial volume, April-August 2013. Data consistent with background only; minimum 90% CL spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross section limit 7.6e-46 cm2 at 33 GeV/c2, in strong disagreement with low-mass WIMP interpretations of other experiments.
result:lux-first-wimp-search-2013.why_it_matters: LUX's first run set the tightest spin-independent WIMP limit of its time and contradicted the low-mass dark matter signals several other experiments had reported, reshaping the field's view of those claims.

claim.quote: A profile-likelihood ratio analysis shows the data to be consistent with a background-only hypothesis, setting new limits on spin-independent WIMP-nucleon, spin-dependent WIMP-neutron, and spin-dependent WIMP-proton cross sections for WIMP masses above 9 GeV/c².

notes: significance is null: this is an exclusion limit, and the collaboration reports no significance for it.
The DOI of the journal version was not fetched in this session, so publication.doi is omitted; the journal reference (Phys. Rev. Lett. 131, 041002 (2023)) comes from the arXiv record.
result:lz-first-wimp-search-2022.summary_technical: SR1: 60 live days, 5.5 t fiducial, 23 Dec 2021 - 11 May 2022. Data consistent with background only; spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross sections above 9.2e-48 cm2 excluded at 90% CL at 36 GeV/c2, with limits also set on spin-dependent WIMP-neutron and WIMP-proton couplings above 9 GeV/c2.
result:lz-first-wimp-search-2022.why_it_matters: LZ's very first 60 days of data already set the world's tightest limit on heavy WIMP dark matter, showing that the detector worked as designed and closing off a large region of parameter space that earlier experiments could not reach.

claim.quote: Dark Matter Search Results from 4.2 Tonne-Years of Exposure of the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) Experiment

notes: significance is null: this is an exclusion limit.
Retrieval of the arXiv abstract for this paper was partial (the fetched rendering paraphrased parts of the abstract); claim.quote is therefore taken from the paper title, which was returned verbatim.
result:lz-ws2024-wimp-search-2024.summary_technical: WS2024: 4.2 ± 0.1 tonne-years (280 live days) with new 214Pb beta tagging and a newly identified 124Xe double-capture recombination background. No excess; leading spin-independent and spin-dependent limits above 9 GeV/c2, reaching 2.2e-48 cm2 at 40 GeV/c2 (median sensitivity 5.1e-48 cm2).
result:lz-ws2024-wimp-search-2024.why_it_matters: With 4.2 tonne-years of data, about twenty times the first run, LZ set the world's strongest limits on heavy WIMP dark matter and demonstrated new background-tagging techniques that the field will need as detectors approach the irreducible neutrino background.

claim.quote: the results are found to be consistent with the nominal electron neutrino rate expectations from the Booster Neutrino Beam and no excess of electron neutrino events is observed

notes: MicroBooNE was built specifically to test the MiniBooNE low-energy excess (result:miniboone-low-energy-excess-2021) using a technology that can distinguish electrons from photons; this 2021 multi-topology search found no corresponding excess.
result:microboone-no-low-energy-excess-2.summary_technical: Using three independent electron-neutrino selections (exclusive two-body 1p, semi-inclusive pionless, fully inclusive), MicroBooNE finds no excess of electron neutrino interactions above the standard-model expectation from the Booster Neutrino Beam, disfavoring a simple electron-like-excess interpretation of the MiniBooNE anomaly.
result:microboone-no-low-energy-excess-2.why_it_matters: This was MicroBooNE's primary physics goal: using liquid-argon imaging to determine whether MiniBooNE's excess was made of electrons (as a sterile-neutrino oscillation would produce) or something else. Finding no excess in any of three independent, differently-systematic analyses disfavors simple electron-flavor explanations of the anomaly.

claim.quote: Here we report the first high-statistics measurement, to our knowledge, of the ν̄μp → μ⁺p n cross-section from the hydrogen atom, using the plastic scintillator target of the MINERvA experiment, extracting FA from free proton targets and measuring the nucleon axial charge radius, rA, to be 0.73 ± 0.17 fm.

notes: The arXiv identifier for this paper was not fetched in this session; the DOI (from the OSTI record) is used as the publication reference.
result:minerva-axial-form-factor-2023.summary_technical: First high-statistics measurement of the ν̄μp→μ⁺n cross-section on free (hydrogen) protons in the MINERvA plastic-scintillator target, avoiding the nuclear-correction uncertainties of deuterium-based extractions; yields the nucleon axial form factor F_A(Q^2) and axial charge radius r_A = 0.73 ± 0.17 fm.
result:minerva-axial-form-factor-2023.why_it_matters: The axial form factor sets the normalization for quasielastic neutrino-nucleon scattering, a dominant interaction channel used by oscillation experiments (MINOS, NOvA, DUNE) to reconstruct neutrino energy; a free-proton measurement removes a major source of nuclear-model uncertainty from that calibration.

claim.quote: A total excess of 638.0 ± 132.8 electron-like events (4.8σ)

An earlier report (Phys. Rev. Lett. 121, 221801 (2018), arXiv:1805.12028, src:miniboone-prl-2018-excess) found a 4.5σ charged-current quasielastic-only excess of 381.2±85.2 events with a smaller exposure; this record uses the 2021 combined/updated figure as the primary claim and cites the 2018 paper as a supporting source.

The 2021 abstract also reports a combined LSND+MiniBooNE significance of 6.0σ, not recorded as this entity's own significance since it is a joint result with a different experiment (LSND, not in this atlas wave).
result:miniboone-low-energy-excess-2021.summary_technical: Combined neutrino- and antineutrino-mode MiniBooNE data (24.11e20 POT total) show a 4.8sigma excess of 638.0+-132.8 low-energy electron-like events over the background-only prediction, updating the original 2018 result. The origin of the excess (sterile neutrinos, a misestimated background, or new physics) remains unresolved; MicroBooNE's 2021 search (result:microboone-no-low-energy-excess-2021) found no corresponding excess in its own single-final-state analyses.
result:miniboone-low-energy-excess-2021.why_it_matters: If it is not an underestimated background, the MiniBooNE excess would require physics beyond the three-neutrino Standard Model, such as a sterile neutrino or new interactions; it motivated the entire Fermilab Short-Baseline Neutrino programme (MicroBooNE, SBND, ICARUS) built to pin down its cause.

claim.quote: Measurement of Neutrino and Antineutrino Oscillations Using Beam and Atmospheric Data in MINOS

result:minos-oscillation-measurement-201.summary_technical: Combined NuMI beam and atmospheric-neutrino analysis: |Δm²|=(2.41+0.09-0.10)x10^-3 eV^2, sin^2(2θ)=0.950+0.035-0.036 (identical ν/ν̄ assumption); separate antineutrino fit gives |Δm̄²|=(2.50+0.23-0.25)x10^-3 eV^2, sin^2(2θ̄)=0.97+0.03-0.08, using 37.88 kton-years of atmospheric data plus beam exposure.
result:minos-oscillation-measurement-201.why_it_matters: Comparing neutrino and antineutrino oscillation parameters from the same detector is a direct test of CPT symmetry and helped establish the precision baseline against which later experiments (MINOS+, NOvA, T2K) measure the same quantities.

claim.quote: No evidence for νμ → νs transitions is found and we set a world-leading limit on θ₂₄ for values of Δm²₄₁ ≲ 1 eV².

notes: experiment_ids lists both experiment:minos and experiment:minos-plus because the analysis uses the combined MINOS/MINOS+ near+far detector data set (1.04 km and 735 km baselines) described in the abstract.
result:minos-sterile-neutrino-limit-2016.summary_technical: Two-detector search for νμ→νs oscillations over 1.04 km and 735 km baselines using a νμ-dominated beam peaked at 3 GeV (10.56x10^20 POT); no evidence found, yielding a world-leading limit on θ_24 for Δm^2_41 <~ 1 eV^2 under a one-sterile-neutrino model with |U_e4|^2=0.
result:minos-sterile-neutrino-limit-2016.why_it_matters: Sterile neutrinos are a leading candidate explanation for the LSND/MiniBooNE anomalies; MINOS's world-leading limit on muon-neutrino disappearance into a sterile state constrained the parameter space available to explain those anomalies via nu_mu-nu_s mixing.

claim.quote: We present new νμ→νe, νμ→νμ, ν̄μ→ν̄e, and ν̄μ→ν̄μ oscillation measurements by the NOvA experiment, with a 50% increase in neutrino-mode beam exposure over the previously reported results.

result:nova-oscillation-parameters-2022.summary_technical: Joint νμ/ν̄μ disappearance and νe/ν̄e appearance fit with 50% more neutrino-mode exposure than the previous NOvA release: Δm²₃₂=(2.41±0.07)×10⁻³ eV², sin²θ₂₃=0.57 (upper octant), normal ordering favored; δ_CP near π/2 excluded at >3σ assuming inverted ordering.
result:nova-oscillation-parameters-2022.why_it_matters: Determining the neutrino mass ordering and the CP-violating phase delta_CP are two of the biggest open questions in neutrino physics; NOvA's beam and atmospheric-scale baseline give it direct sensitivity to both, in combination with results from other experiments such as T2K.

claim.quote: Evidence for oscillation of atmospheric neutrinos

result:sk-atmospheric-oscillation-eviden.summary_technical: 33.0 kiloton-year exposure; observed a zenith-angle-dependent muon-neutrino deficit inconsistent with the no-oscillation expectation, consistent with two-flavour nu_mu <-> nu_tau oscillation. The collaboration's own title states 'evidence', not 'discovery' or 'observation'.
result:sk-atmospheric-oscillation-eviden.why_it_matters: The result that first convinced the field neutrinos oscillate (and hence have mass), contradicting the Standard Model's massless-neutrino assumption; foundational to the 2015 Nobel Prize in Physics (shared with SNO).

claim.quote: We report the first search result for the flux of astrophysical electron antineutrinos for energies O(10) MeV in the gadolinium-loaded Super-Kamiokande (SK) detector. ... No significant excess over the expected background in the observed events is found for the neutrino energies below 31.3 MeV. Thus, the flux upper limits are placed at the 90% confidence level.

result:sk-gd-first-antineutrino-search-2.summary_technical: First SK-Gd physics result: 22.5x552 kiloton-day exposure at 0.01wt% Gd, searching for astrophysical electron antineutrinos (E<31.3 MeV) via inverse beta decay with enhanced neutron tagging. No significant excess found; flux upper limits set at 90% CL, already comparable to the prior pure-water SK limit despite far less exposure.
result:sk-gd-first-antineutrino-search-2.why_it_matters: The first physics result from the gadolinium-loaded SK-Gd phase, demonstrating that neutron tagging works as designed and that SK-Gd's ultimate goal - detecting the diffuse supernova neutrino background - is within reach with more exposure.

claim.quote: Solar neutrino measurements using the full data period of Super-Kamiokande-IV

notes: key_value and part of key_value_text rely on a WebFetch-summarised reading of the abstract rather than a verbatim quoted number, because the raw abstract text could not be extracted character-for-character in this session; confidence is set to 'approximate' accordingly.
result:sk-solar-neutrino-measurement-202.summary_technical: Combines SK-I through SK-IV (5,805 live days total); SK-IV alone contributes 2,970 days (Oct. 2008 - May 2018) and 65,443 solar-neutrino events. Reports an 8B solar-neutrino flux and oscillation parameters (sin^2 theta_12, Delta m^2_21) in mild tension with the complementary KamLAND reactor measurement.
result:sk-solar-neutrino-measurement-202.why_it_matters: Super-Kamiokande's most precise, longest-baseline solar-neutrino measurement, testing the MSW-LMA solar-oscillation solution and probing for any energy-dependent deviation (the 'upturn') that would signal new physics beyond standard three-flavour oscillation.

claim.quote: We currently hold the world record for the highest instantaneous luminosity ever achieved at a particle accelerator: 5.319 x 1034 cm−2s−1 achieved on June 30, 2026.

notes: Earlier milestones on the same machine, not recorded as separate results: 2.22 × 10³⁴ cm⁻² s⁻¹ on 15 June 2020 (KEK IPNS press release, the first time SuperKEKB passed KEKB's 2.11 × 10³⁴) and 5.1 × 10³⁴ cm⁻² s⁻¹ quoted in the March 2025 Belle II European Strategy input.
Attributed to experiment:belle-ii because the atlas has no result owner for a bare accelerator; the machine is accelerator:superkekb.
result:superkekb-luminosity-world-record.summary_technical: SuperKEKB reached a peak instantaneous luminosity of 5.319 × 10³⁴ cm⁻² s⁻¹, the highest achieved by any colliding-beam accelerator, using the nano-beam scheme with a large crossing angle.
result:superkekb-luminosity-world-record.why_it_matters: Instantaneous luminosity sets the rate at which Belle II accumulates its data set; the record is the operational proof of the nano-beam scheme on which the 50 ab⁻¹ programme depends.

claim.quote: Here the T2K collaboration reports a measurement that favors large enhancement of the neutrino oscillation probability, excluding values of dCP which result in a large enhancement of the observed anti-neutrino oscillation probability at three standard deviations (3 sigma). ... Our results show an indication of CP violation in the lepton sector.

result:t2k-cp-violation-constraint-2020.summary_technical: Combined neutrino- and antineutrino-mode appearance/disappearance data exclude CP-conserving delta_CP values (0, +/-pi) at 3 sigma; 3-sigma interval [-3.41,-0.03] (normal ordering) or [-2.54,-0.32] (inverted ordering). The collaboration's own wording is 'an indication of CP violation in the lepton sector', reproduced verbatim in the claim quote; not classified as 'evidence' or 'discovery' to avoid inflating beyond the paper's own language (v0.2 rule 7 / A16).
result:t2k-cp-violation-constraint-2020.why_it_matters: The first constraint on the leptonic CP-violating phase delta_CP from any single experiment, disfavouring CP conservation at 3 sigma and pointing towards a possible explanation (leptogenesis) for the universe's matter-antimatter asymmetry; the physics case for Hyper-Kamiokande's more sensitive CP search.

claim.quote: The T2K experiment has observed electron neutrino appearance in a muon neutrino beam produced 295 km from the Super-Kamiokande detector with a peak energy of 0.6 GeV. A total of 28 electron neutrino events were detected with an energy distribution consistent with an appearance signal, corresponding to a significance of 7.3σ when compared to 4.92 ± 0.55 expected background events.

result:t2k-electron-neutrino-appearance-.summary_technical: 28 nu_e candidate events at Super-Kamiokande vs. 4.92+/-0.55 expected background; 7.3 sigma significance. Best-fit sin^2(2 theta_13)=0.140(+0.038/-0.032) (normal ordering) at delta_CP=0, combined with reactor theta_13 measurements to begin constraining delta_CP.
result:t2k-electron-neutrino-appearance-.why_it_matters: The first observation (as opposed to indication) of muon-to-electron neutrino appearance at an accelerator, confirming that theta_13 is sizeable and opening the direct search for leptonic CP violation that culminated in T2K's 2020 delta_CP constraint.

claim.quote: The T2K experiment observes indications of νμ→νe appearance in data accumulated with 1.43×10²⁰ protons on target. Six events pass all selection criteria at the far detector. ... the probability to observe six or more candidate events is 7×10⁻³, equivalent to 2.5σ significance.

result:t2k-electron-neutrino-indication-.summary_technical: Six candidate nu_e-appearance events observed at Super-Kamiokande with 1.43e20 protons on target, against an expected background of 1.5+/-0.3 events; probability of a background-only fluctuation 7e-3 (2.5 sigma). Constrains sin^2(2 theta_13) to 0.03(0.04)-0.28(0.34) at 90% CL. The collaboration's own title says 'indication', a weaker claim than 'evidence' or 'observation'; classified here as result_type 'measurement' because the ontology's result_type enum has no 'indication' tier and 2.5 sigma is below the conventional ~3 sigma evidence threshold.
result:t2k-electron-neutrino-indication-.why_it_matters: The first experimental hint, from any experiment, that theta_13 might be non-zero and that muon-to-electron neutrino appearance is observable at an accelerator; motivated the reactor experiments (Daya Bay, RENO, Double Chooz) that soon confirmed theta_13 != 0, and set up T2K's own later observation (2014) and CP-violation search (2020).

claim.quote: Experimental Observation of Isolated Large Transverse Energy Electrons with Associated Missing Energy at sqrt(s)=540 GeV

result:ua1-w-boson-observation-1983.summary_technical: UA1 Collaboration, Phys. Lett. B 122 (1983) 103-116; isolated high-transverse-energy electrons with missing transverse energy at sqrt(s)=540 GeV, interpreted as p-pbar -> W(+/-) + X, W -> e + nu, with the electron-neutrino system consistent with a particle of mass ~80 GeV/c^2. Announced at a CERN press conference on 25 January 1983.
result:ua1-w-boson-observation-1983.why_it_matters: The first direct evidence for the W boson, the carrier of the weak nuclear force, confirming a central prediction of the electroweak theory that unifies electromagnetism and the weak interaction.

claim.quote: Experimental Observation of Lepton Pairs of Invariant Mass Around 95 GeV/c^2 at the CERN SPS Collider

result:ua1-z-boson-observation-1983.summary_technical: UA1 Collaboration, Phys. Lett. B 126 (1983) 398-410; four e+e- pairs and one mu+mu- pair with invariant mass around 95 GeV/c^2, interpreted as Z0 -> l+ l-.
result:ua1-z-boson-observation-1983.why_it_matters: The first direct observation of the Z boson, the neutral carrier of the weak force, completing the experimental confirmation of the electroweak theory's predicted force carriers alongside the W.

claim.quote: Observation of Single Isolated Electrons of High Transverse Momentum in Events with Missing Transverse Energy at the CERN anti-p p Collider

result:ua2-w-boson-observation-1983.summary_technical: UA2 Collaboration, Phys. Lett. B 122 (1983) 476-485; four candidate events with a single isolated high-p_T electron and missing transverse energy, consistent with p-pbar -> W(+/-) + anything, W -> e + nu. UA2 physicist Luigi Di Lella announced the result at a CERN seminar on 22 January 1983, three days before the joint public announcement.
result:ua2-w-boson-observation-1983.why_it_matters: An independent confirmation of the W boson using a very different detector design (calorimetry rather than a magnetic spectrometer), establishing the discovery beyond a single experiment's systematics.

claim.quote: Evidence for Z0 -> e+ e- at the CERN anti-p p Collider

result:ua2-z-boson-evidence-1983.summary_technical: UA2 Collaboration, Phys. Lett. B 129 (1983) 130-140; eight Z0 -> e+e- candidate events giving a Z boson mass of 91.9 +/- 1.3 (stat) +/- 1.4 (syst) GeV/c^2. Titled 'Evidence for', a more cautious claim than UA1's 'Observation'.
result:ua2-z-boson-evidence-1983.why_it_matters: A second, independent sighting of the Z boson using UA2's calorimeter-based design, with a mass measurement (91.9 GeV/c^2) consistent with UA1's, reinforcing the electroweak theory's prediction.

topic:accelerator-dark-matter-searches.overview: Accelerator searches assume dark-matter particles escape the detector without interacting, leaving missing energy and momentum. At the LHC, ATLAS and CMS look for an imbalance in transverse momentum recoiling against a Standard Model particle, for bumps in dijet or dilepton mass spectra from a mediator, and for excesses in dijet angular distributions; no signal has been seen and limits are set on masses, couplings and cross sections. Fixed-target experiments increasingly probe lighter, sub-GeV dark sectors, where thermal relic targets are sharp and largely model-independent. A collider signal alone cannot prove that what was produced is the cosmological dark matter.

topic:astroparticle-physics.overview: Astroparticle physics uses the universe as a laboratory. Cosmic rays are a non-thermal population pervading the universe, with charged-particle energies from tens of MeV to close to 1 ZeV; gamma rays and high-energy neutrinos are detected alongside them, and combining these messengers with gravitational waves is called multi-messenger astrophysics. Instruments include extensive air-shower arrays, atmospheric fluorescence detectors, imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes, cubic-kilometre neutrino telescopes in ice and water, and space-borne spectrometers. Central questions are the origin of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays, the identity of the sources of astrophysical neutrinos, and astrophysical signatures of dark matter and of new light particles.

topic:atmospheric-neutrinos.overview: Cosmic rays interacting in the atmosphere produce mesons whose decays yield muon and electron neutrinos and antineutrinos over a very wide energy range and over baselines from a few tens of kilometres for downward-going neutrinos to the Earth diameter for upward-going ones. Because the same detector sees both, the zenith-angle and energy dependence of the observed rates maps the oscillation pattern directly. Atmospheric samples constrain the atmospheric mixing angle and mass-squared difference, and, through matter effects during passage through the Earth, carry sensitivity to the neutrino mass ordering. Flux predictions rely on cosmic-ray spectra and hadronic-interaction models.

topic:axions-alps.overview: Axions and axion-like particles are hypothetical light bosons arising from the spontaneous breaking of a global symmetry; a small explicit breaking gives them mass. The QCD axion, from the Peccei-Quinn mechanism, is of particular interest because it offers a compelling scheme to preserve CP symmetry in QCD, and the cold dark matter of the universe may consist of axions. Couplings to Standard Model particles are suppressed by the symmetry-breaking scale, so the particles interact very weakly and detecting them would open a window on physics far beyond accelerator reach. Searches run in laboratories, in stars and in the Galactic halo.

topic:b-physics.overview: The b quark is the lighter member of the third-generation doublet, so b-flavored hadrons decay through generation-changing transitions; loop and box diagrams, flavor oscillations and large CP asymmetries are all accessible. Measurements cover production and spectroscopy, lifetimes, mixing, hadronic, rare hadronic and electroweak-penguin decays. Semileptonic decays determine the CKM elements Vcb and Vub, where inclusive and exclusive determinations remain inconsistent enough that the Particle Data Group scales the averaged uncertainty. Measured b to s lepton-pair branching fractions sit consistently below Standard Model expectations, while lepton-universality ratios, once discrepant, are now consistent after a background reassessment.

topic:cevns.overview: In coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering a low-energy neutrino scatters from a nucleus acting as a single particle. The total cross section is large by neutrino standards, but the process eluded detection for four decades because the nuclear recoil deposits only about a keV. COHERENT observed it at 6.7 sigma in 2017 using a 14.6 kg caesium-iodide scintillator at the Oak Ridge Spallation Neutron Source, and derived improved constraints on non-standard neutrino interactions with quarks. The process bears on nuclear structure and astrophysics as well as particle physics, and sets an irreducible neutrino background for dark-matter detectors.

topic:charm-physics.overview: Charm hadrons provide the only accessible up-type-quark system in which meson mixing and CP violation can be studied. A meson created as a D0 time-evolves into a D0-bar, and the mixing parameters are measured to be small and positive. CP violation in decay has been established in the difference of asymmetries for D0 to K+K- and D0 to pi+pi-, with the Particle Data Group quoting (-0.159 +/- 0.029) per cent. Interpretation is limited because long-distance contributions are not calculable from first principles. Charm decays also provide decay constants, form factors and precise Vcs and Vcd.

topic:collider-bsm-searches.overview: Direct searches look for hypothetical new particles produced in collisions and identified by their decay products. Supersymmetry, one of the most studied extensions, would pair every Standard Model fermion and gauge boson with a partner differing by half a unit of spin: squarks, sleptons, gluinos, and the charginos and neutralinos formed by mixing gauginos with higgsinos. Since no such particle has been seen, supersymmetry would have to be broken. Other targets include heavy gauge bosons, leptoquarks, vector-like quarks, extra Higgs bosons, extra dimensions and compositeness. Results are reported as cross-section limits interpreted in simplified or complete models.

topic:collider-physics.overview: Collider physics studies particle collisions at the highest centre-of-mass energies reachable in the laboratory. LHC Run 3 began in July 2022 at 13.6 TeV, building on electron-positron data from LEP and SLC and on the proton-antiproton Tevatron programme. The field combines precision Standard Model measurements - of the Higgs boson, the electroweak sector, the top quark and QCD - with direct searches for new particles. Events are reconstructed as jets, leptons, photons and missing transverse momentum and compared with perturbative predictions. The Snowmass 2021 Energy Frontier report and the 2023 P5 report set out the next steps, including the High-Luminosity LHC and a proposed offshore Higgs factory.

topic:cosmic-rays.overview: Cosmic rays are a non-thermal population of particles pervading the universe, characterised by their spectrum, composition and arrival directions. Charged cosmic rays extend from tens of MeV to close to 1 ZeV, with an intensity of about 10^4 per square metre per second per steradian above 1 GeV and a steeply falling power-law spectrum. The striking spectral features are the knee at a few PeV, where the index changes from about 2.7 to about 3, a second knee near 100 PeV, and the ankle at a few EeV; the flux is largely suppressed above a few tens of EeV. Arrival directions are mostly isotropic.

topic:cp-violation.overview: CP combines charge conjugation with parity. The weak interactions violate C and P maximally but preserve CP in most processes; CP violation appears in interference effects, discovered in neutral kaon decays in 1964 and established later in B decays (2001) and D decays (2019). In the Standard Model all quark-sector CP violation follows from one irreducible phase of the unitary CKM matrix, whose unitarity relations form triangles. Experiments test whether magnitudes measured in semileptonic and leptonic decays and mixing, and angles measured from CP asymmetries, describe a single consistent triangle.

topic:dark-matter.overview: Cosmological models include a non-baryonic, electromagnetically near-neutral matter species with negligible velocity, generically called cold dark matter. In the benchmark LambdaCDM fit adopted by the Particle Data Group it accounts for 26.4 per cent of the critical density and 84.4 per cent of the total matter density; only a small fraction of the non-baryonic content, the three Standard Model neutrinos, is identified. Its particle nature is hypothetical. Searches follow three complementary strategies - direct detection of Galactic dark matter scattering underground, indirect detection of annihilation or decay products, and production at accelerators. No non-gravitational detection has been established.

topic:dark-photons-dark-sectors.overview: A dark sector is a set of hypothetical particles neutral under the Standard Model forces, connected to ordinary matter only through weak portal interactions. The dark photon is a conjectured gauge boson of such a sector, detectable through kinetic mixing with the ordinary photon; vector, Higgs and neutrino portals and axion-like-particle portals are the minimal renormalizable or dimension-five options. Because such sectors are generically weakly coupled and can naturally have MeV-to-GeV masses while respecting Standard Model symmetries, they are only mildly constrained by high-energy collider data, and intensity-frontier experiments, including those on neutrino beams, offer the strongest reach.

topic:detector-rd.overview: Detector research and development turns measurement requirements into working technology. The Particle Data Group review chapters catalogue the working principles and performance of the main families: vacuum, gaseous, solid-state and superconducting photon detectors; organic and inorganic scintillators; Cherenkov, gaseous and transition-radiation detectors; time projection chambers including liquid-argon ones; large rare-event time projection chambers; sub-kelvin detectors; and low-radioactivity background techniques. The Snowmass 2021 Instrumentation Frontier report groups the needed research and development for collider, neutrino, rare-process and cosmic experiments and lays out priority areas for keeping that capability healthy.

topic:direct-dark-matter-detection.overview: Direct detection looks for nuclear or electron recoils left when Galactic dark matter passes through a low-background detector operated deep underground. Interpretation needs the local dark-matter density and velocity distribution, which are themselves uncertain at the level of a factor of a few. Dual-phase liquid-xenon time projection chambers currently lead for masses around tens of GeV: the Particle Data Group tabulates a spin-independent cross-section limit of 2.2 x 10^-48 cm^2 near 40 GeV from LUX-ZEPLIN, with XENONnT and PandaX-4T close behind. Sensitivity is approaching the irreducible background from coherent neutrino scattering, which those detectors have now begun to observe.

topic:electroweak-physics.overview: The electroweak Standard Model is a renormalizable gauge theory based on SU(2) x U(1). Because the W and Z masses, the Higgs and top masses, the electromagnetic and strong couplings and the weak mixing angle are related through radiative corrections, a global fit tests the theory at the quantum level. Inputs include low-energy observables, Z-pole lineshape parameters and asymmetries from LEP and SLC, W and Z masses and widths and W and Z decays. The Particle Data Group fit does not include the CDF Run II W-mass measurement, which dominates the tension among direct determinations.

topic:flavor-physics.overview: Flavor physics studies transitions between the three generations of quarks and leptons. In the Standard Model the masses and mixings of quarks have a common origin in the Yukawa interactions with the Higgs condensate, and quark flavor change is governed by the unitary Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix, which carries three real parameters and one complex phase. Flavor-changing neutral currents arise only through loops, so meson mixing, rare decays and CP asymmetries in kaon, charm and beauty hadrons are sensitive to hypothetical new particles far above direct collider reach - the Snowmass Rare Processes and Precision Frontier report quotes scales up to thousands of TeV.

topic:gamma-rays.overview: Gamma rays trace non-thermal processes and identify sites where particles are accelerated. The Particle Data Group counts roughly 6660 catalogued sources above 50 MeV and about 300 at TeV energies, plus diffuse Galactic and extragalactic emission that largely follows power laws. Space-borne pair-conversion telescopes cover the MeV-GeV range; above about 100 GeV the flux is too low for satellites, so ground-based imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes and particle-detector arrays observe the air showers gamma rays initiate. Observations address particle acceleration in supernova remnants, pulsars, binaries, active galaxies and gamma-ray bursts, and are also used to search for new physics.

topic:heavy-ion-physics-qgp.overview: Heavy-ion collisions quickly form a droplet of quark-gluon plasma with a remarkably small viscosity - the hottest and smallest droplet of liquid made on Earth. The physics spans highly energetic quarks and gluons described by perturbative QCD down to a bath of strongly interacting gluons at lower energy scales; those gluons thermalize quickly and form the plasma, while energetic partons traverse it and emerge as jets. Analysing the final particles in different ways probes the plasma properties and the multi-scale QCD dynamics governing its formation and evolution. The Snowmass Energy Frontier report stresses the connection to nuclear structure and the nuclear medium.

topic:heavy-neutral-leptons.overview: Non-zero neutrino masses point to the likely existence of additional Standard Model neutral fermions. When such hypothetical states are heavy enough that they cannot be produced in oscillations they are called heavy neutral leptons. They would mix with the active neutrinos and could be produced in meson and tau decays, in beam dumps and at colliders, then decay to visible final states after a possibly macroscopic flight distance. Searches span beta decay, accelerator experiments and colliders, and are complemented by astrophysical and cosmological constraints; the parameter space is usually presented as mixing angle versus mass for each lepton flavour.

topic:higgs-physics.overview: Electroweak symmetry breaking posits a self-interacting complex scalar doublet whose CP-even neutral component acquires a vacuum expectation value of about 246 GeV; the remaining component is the Higgs boson, discovered at the LHC in 2012 with a mass near 125 GeV. Measurements cover inclusive, differential and simplified-template cross sections in each production and decay channel, couplings expressed in the kappa framework or as effective field theory coefficients, the mass, the width, and spin and CP properties. The Higgs self-coupling and possible exotic or beyond-Standard-Model Higgs decays remain open.

topic:high-energy-astrophysical-neutrino.overview: Astrophysical neutrinos have energies far beyond those of solar, supernova, atmospheric and accelerator neutrinos, and probe fundamental physics from the TeV to the EeV scale and beyond. Because they are weakly interacting and electrically neutral they escape regions opaque to electromagnetic radiation and point back to their sources, carrying unique information about extreme non-thermal environments. The Particle Data Group notes that the observed distribution is largely isotropic, with evidence for two extragalactic sources and for a contribution from the Galactic plane. Detection uses cubic-kilometre Cherenkov arrays in ice and water, with radio and air-shower techniques targeting the highest energies.

topic:indirect-dark-matter-detection.overview: Indirect detection looks for Standard Model particles produced by hypothetical dark-matter annihilation or decay in astrophysical environments, using photons, charged cosmic rays and neutrinos. Substantial advances in observational data sets, complemented by numerical simulations, have enabled strong constraints on particle models and revealed several intriguing hints of possible signals whose astrophysical interpretation remains debated. Targets include dwarf spheroidal galaxies, the Galactic Centre, galaxy clusters, the Sun and the diffuse background. Limits depend strongly on the assumed dark-matter density profile of the target and on the modelling of astrophysical backgrounds and cosmic-ray propagation.

topic:instrumentation.overview: Instrumentation covers the sensors, electronics, readout and analysis techniques that set what an experiment can measure. The Particle Data Group treats accelerator and non-accelerator detectors in separate review chapters covering photon detectors, organic and inorganic scintillators, Cherenkov and gaseous detectors, liquid-argon time projection chambers, air-shower and atmospheric-fluorescence detectors, neutrino telescopes, sub-kelvin detectors and low-radioactivity background techniques. The Snowmass 2021 Instrumentation Frontier report organises the research and development needed for future collider, neutrino, rare-process and cosmic experiments, and identifies priority areas for sustaining that capability.

topic:lepton-flavor-violation.overview: Charged lepton flavour violating transitions would be a clear signal of physics beyond the Standard Model, in which they are forbidden or utterly negligible. Searches cover a variety of channels, the most sensitive involving muons - radiative decay to an electron and a photon, decay to three electrons, and conversion to an electron in the field of a nucleus - as well as tau decays and transitions of heavier states. No positive evidence has been found. The Snowmass topical group report notes that these processes already probe mass scales up to thousands of TeV, so an observation would be unambiguous evidence of new particles.

topic:long-lived-particles.overview: Particles beyond the Standard Model can generically have lifetimes long compared with weak-scale Standard Model particles. Produced at the LHC, such long-lived particles would decay far from the primary proton-proton interaction vertex, giving signatures unlike those of the promptly decaying particles most searches target. Identifying them needs customized techniques: significantly displaced decay vertices, tracks with atypical properties, and short track segments. A joint effort by theorists and the ATLAS, CMS and LHCb collaborations, together with dedicated experiments such as MoEDAL, milliQan, MATHUSLA, CODEX-b and FASER, has surveyed the signature space to avoid overlooking discovery avenues.

topic:multimessenger-astrophysics.overview: Multimessenger astrophysics combines photons, gravitational waves, neutrinos and cosmic rays, which carry inherently complementary information about individual cosmic sources and about source populations. The Particle Data Group describes combined observations of charged cosmic rays, gamma rays, neutrinos and gravitational waves as giving valuable insight into the most extreme astrophysical environments. Key achievements include measuring the ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray spectrum to the highest observable energies, discovering the diffuse high-energy neutrino background, the first direct gravitational-wave detections, and the first joint electromagnetic and gravitational-wave identification. The practical challenge is rapid alert distribution and follow-up across observatories.

topic:muon-precision-physics.overview: Quantum loop effects make the muon magnetic moment deviate slightly from the Dirac value, and the anomaly can be both measured in storage rings and predicted precisely, testing the Standard Model at loop level. After the final Fermilab E989 result the experimental world average is 116 592 071.5(14.5) x 10^-11, against a Standard Model prediction of 116 592 033(62) x 10^-11 compiled by the Muon g-2 Theory Initiative; the difference, 38(63) x 10^-11, is compatible with zero and now dominated by theory uncertainty. A permanent electric dipole moment would directly signal time-reversal and, assuming CPT, CP violation; only upper limits exist.

topic:neutrino-interactions.overview: Neutrino cross sections are an essential ingredient of every neutrino experiment, and uncertainties in neutrino-nucleus scattering remain a dominant systematic in oscillation measurements. The Particle Data Group surveys measurements from roughly 0.1 to 1000 GeV with emphasis on inclusive, deep inelastic, quasi-elastic and resonance-production processes on a range of nuclear targets. Nuclear effects distort the observed kinematics and bias reconstructed neutrino energy, so precise flux estimates, theoretical input and complementary electron-nucleus scattering data are all needed. Modern measurements come from ArgoNeuT, ICARUS, MicroBooNE, MINERvA, NOvA, T2K, IceCube and FASERnu, among others.

topic:neutrino-mass-direct.overview: Oscillations fix only mass-squared differences, so the absolute scale must come from elsewhere. The only model-independent information comes from energy-momentum conservation in weak decays: a non-zero mass distorts the beta spectrum near its endpoint, and tritium is favoured because its decay energy is small. KATRIN has found no indication of a non-zero mass and sets an upper limit of 0.45 eV at 90 per cent confidence, improving on the roughly 2.2 eV bounds from Mainz and Troitsk, and should approach a sensitivity near 0.3 eV. Holmium-163 electron-capture calorimetry and cyclotron-radiation spectroscopy are complementary approaches.

topic:neutrino-oscillations.overview: Neutrino flavour oscillations follow from neutrinos having mass and from flavour states being superpositions of mass states, described by a lepton mixing matrix with three angles, one Dirac CP phase and, for Majorana neutrinos, two further phases. Two independent mass-squared differences are measured. Solar, atmospheric, accelerator and reactor experiments each constrain different combinations, and propagation through matter modifies the pattern, notably through the Mikheyev-Smirnov-Wolfenstein effect for solar neutrinos. A combined three-neutrino analysis leaves the mass ordering, the octant of the largest atmospheric angle, and the size of leptonic CP violation as the principal open questions.

topic:neutrino-physics.overview: Neutrino physics addresses the least understood Standard Model fermions. Oscillation experiments established that neutrinos have mass and mix, which the minimal Standard Model does not accommodate; oscillations depend only on mass-squared differences, so the absolute mass scale and the Dirac or Majorana nature must be probed by other means. Sources span reactors, accelerator beams, the Sun, the atmosphere, supernovae, the Earth and distant cosmic accelerators, covering more than twenty orders of magnitude in energy. Detection uses charged-current and neutral-current scattering in large water, ice, scintillator and liquid-argon detectors, and precision spectroscopy of weak decays.

topic:neutrinoless-double-beta-decay.overview: Neutrinoless double beta decay is a hypothetical ultra-rare nuclear decay that would violate total lepton number by two units and require neutrinos to be Majorana particles. Under the assumption that Majorana neutrino mass is the only low-energy source of lepton-number violation, the half-life relates to an effective Majorana mass through phase space and nuclear matrix elements, whose uncertainty spreads the inferred mass by a factor of two to three; other new-physics mechanisms could dominate instead. No decay has been seen. The strongest limits come from xenon-136 and germanium-76, exceeding 10^26 years.

topic:nuclear-and-heavy-ion.overview: This area covers the interface between nuclear and particle physics where the questions are materially particle-physics questions: quantum chromodynamics at extreme temperature and density in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, and the structure of nucleons and nuclei. Heavy-ion collisions quickly form a droplet of quark-gluon plasma with a remarkably small viscosity; energetic partons traversing that plasma emerge as jets whose modification probes its properties. The Snowmass Energy Frontier QCD and heavy-ion report emphasises the connections to nucleon structure and to the Electron-Ion Collider. Low-energy nuclear structure and applied nuclear science are outside the atlas scope.

topic:precision-and-rare-processes.overview: This area covers searches for extremely rare processes and for tiny deviations from the Standard Model, studied with intense sources and high-precision detectors. Quantum corrections from hypothetical heavy or feebly interacting states shift observables such as the muon anomalous magnetic moment, electric dipole moments and rare-decay rates, so measurements at the part-per-billion or 10^-13 branching-fraction level probe mass scales far above collider energies. The same facilities search directly for light, long-lived or feebly coupled states - heavy neutral leptons, dark photons and other long-lived particles - at beam dumps, fixed-target experiments and the forward regions of colliders.

topic:qcd.overview: Quantum chromodynamics is the SU(3) gauge field theory describing the strong interactions of coloured quarks and gluons within the Standard Model. Its coupling runs, so hard scattering is computed perturbatively while confinement and hadron structure need lattice QCD or non-perturbative modelling. The Particle Data Group review organises experimental QCD around hadronic final-state observables and collider measurements, and determines the strong coupling from hadronic tau decays, heavy-quarkonium decays, parton-distribution fits, electron-positron final states, hadron-collider observables, the electroweak precision fit and lattice QCD, which are then combined into a world average.

topic:rare-kaon-physics.overview: Rare kaon decays divide into searches for explicit Standard Model violations, the golden modes, other constraints on Standard Model parameters, and studies of low-energy strong interactions. The golden modes K+ to pi+ neutrino antineutrino and K_L to pi0 neutrino antineutrino are dominated by short-distance physics and calculable with negligible theoretical uncertainty. NA62 at the CERN SPS reported in 2026, using data through 2024, a branching fraction of 9.6 (+1.9/-1.8) x 10^-11 against a Standard Model estimate of (8.2 +/- 0.6) x 10^-11; KOTO at J-PARC pursues the neutral mode. Lepton-flavor and lepton-number violating kaon decays are also searched for.

topic:reactor-neutrinos.overview: Nuclear reactors are intense sources of electron antineutrinos from the beta decays of fission fragments, detected mainly through inverse beta decay in liquid scintillator. Reactor antineutrinos provided the first direct detection of the neutrino, and later experiments found clear evidence for oscillation, giving unique input to neutrino mass and mixing. Kilometre-baseline experiments measured the smallest mixing angle, and a medium-baseline detector about 53 km from two Chinese power plants is designed to determine the mass ordering from the fine structure of the disappearance spectrum. Ongoing questions include reactor flux and spectrum predictions and short-baseline searches for hypothetical sterile states.

topic:solar-neutrinos.overview: The Sun produces energy through two main chains, the proton-proton chain and the CNO cycle, each emitting electron neutrinos with characteristic spectra; mean energies are low, with the pp neutrinos carrying only a fraction of an MeV. Radiochemical and water-Cherenkov experiments found fewer electron neutrinos than the standard solar model predicts, which is explained by flavour conversion, enhanced inside the Sun by the Mikheyev-Smirnov-Wolfenstein matter effect. Borexino, a liquid-scintillator detector at Gran Sasso operating from 2007 to 2021, made the first real-time measurements of several low-energy components, including the CNO neutrinos.

topic:sterile-neutrinos.overview: Sterile neutrinos are hypothetical neutral fermions without Standard Model gauge interactions that could mix with the three active neutrinos; the Particle Data Group treats light sterile states as one way of extending the Standard Model to give neutrinos mass, and devotes a section to additional neutrinos at the eV scale. Four canonical short-baseline anomalies - from decay-at-rest and decay-in-flight accelerator experiments, from reactors and from radioactive-source gallium measurements - remain unresolved, and the Snowmass white paper argues that disappearance and appearance data do not fit consistently within a minimal 3+1 picture. Heavier sterile states are candidate dark matter.

topic:supernova-neutrinos.overview: Neutrinos govern the infall of a collapsing stellar core, help trigger and fuel the explosion, and drive the cooling and deleptonization of the newly formed neutron star, so they offer the only direct probe of conditions at the centre of a supernova. A core-collapse supernova produces a burst of neutrinos of all flavours in the few-tens-of-MeV range over seconds. Extracting source properties requires separating them from effects imprinted on the way out: self-induced flavour conversion from neutrino-neutrino interactions in the deepest regions, and matter effects in the envelope. Neutrinos from past cosmic supernovae form a diffuse background that is also observable in principle.

topic:top-physics.overview: The top quark is the weak-isospin partner of the bottom quark, with a mass of about 172.5 GeV and therefore a Yukawa coupling of order unity. Being heavier than the W boson it is the only quark that decays weakly into a real W and a b quark, and its lifetime is shorter than the timescale of non-perturbative strong interactions, so it does not hadronize and its spin information survives into its decay products. Abundant LHC production enables precise measurements of the mass, couplings, production cross sections and branching ratios; the Particle Data Group notes a 1.7-sigma tension between the top-quark mass inferred indirectly from the electroweak fit and the value combined directly from LHC measurements.
